question: Which canonical text, editing and syntax-presentation contract should native code blocks use?
trigger: User challenged whether CodeMirror had already been done and explicitly requested history reconciliation followed by best-api-review audit code. Read-only product audit with local research recording.
requirements: Reconcile earlier CodeMirror, external-text and native performance work before selecting a new direction; preserve rejected experiments and dated proof limits.
Cover all 13 code source groups and eight semantic units, including native/static, external-only, mixed and authored consumers.
Preserve one canonical newline-bearing Text, exact schema identity, selection, history, clipboard/codec content, annotations and collaboration ownership.
Keep optional renderer/parser dependencies explicit; preserve native full-DOM and authored rich-projection jobs without adding a second canonical state owner.
Challenge deletion, merger, reuse and replacement alternatives, including cutting intermediate insertion, hidden grammar mutation and JSON-only package policy.
Record evidence and verdict without product implementation, a downstream implementation plan, publication or fresh browser/performance claims.
evidenceReuse: Re-read the prior code decision and Sep4/Sep5 records, Sep2 model plan, Sep3/Sep4 external-text executions, Sep6 final R4 native adoption and Sep15 external-text review/recovered execution. Two bounded native subagents inspected CodeMirror/history and native syntax; the lead inspected commands, codecs, consumers and proof. Current code partition passed 58 tests/142 assertions. Two targeted observational probes with eight assertions executed against current source. Historical browser/timing claims were preserved as historical rather than rerun or promoted.
summary: Pursue bounded code-command and native-highlighter cleanup while retaining one Text, native/static rendering, optional CodeMirror and synchronous external-text ownership. Cut hidden Python registry mutation and accidental grammar API, reuse schema-owned construction instead of public defaultType plus paragraph retyping, move JSON-only formatting policy to copied UI with selection-preserving canonical edits, repair selected-line endpoints, and remove native backend initialization from shared CodeMirror controls. All 13 source groups and eight semantic units reviewed; current probes expose selection loss, invalid intermediate schema, extra-line indentation and alias-cache disagreement. CodeMirror/parser adoption and later native R4 improvements were already done; the old ledger summary was incomplete.

alternatives: Make CodeMirror the sole renderer: Stop. Native full-DOM, static and authored rich-projection consumers have independent current jobs. CodeMirror search/print already exist and are not arguments against it.

Delete CodeMirror or expose canonical editor internals to its adapter: Stop. Existing bounded-DOM code editing needs its mounted parser/input owner; the narrow optional protocol already carries canonical changes, history and neutral paint.
Merge native syntax into structural code editing: Stop. Plain and CodeMirror-only consumers omit it, while native/static and mixed views require it.

Delete native decoration projection and inline it into each kit: Stop. Duplicates token projection and lifecycle machinery. Delete hidden caller-registry mutation and unused backend initialization instead.

Keep current custom defaultType construction and JSON format command: Pursue the stronger cut. Schema insertion already owns construction; copied JSON policy can use canonical edits. Current probes demonstrate schema rejection and no-op selection loss.
Add shared code-text recipes, a generic formatter manager or a new scheduler/cache owner: Stop. No independent current job justifies the protocol; prior execution rejected shared recipes.

Replace Lowlight with one incremental parser everywhere: unaccepted alternative pending current matched whole-operation/language/SSR evidence. No runtime speed claim or parser replacement is selected.
Keep everything and configure callers around it: reject. Hidden resource mutation and command-owned selection loss require repair at their owners.
proofLimits: Audit complete; cleanup not implemented. Current model-level evidence is 58 existing unit tests and two observational probes characterizing undesirable behavior. No browser/device/physical IME/assistive-tech, fresh CodeMirror integration run, packed-distribution or bundle measurement, or new performance comparison ran. Historical R4 and external-text receipts retain their original source/cohort limitations and historical-unbound execution status. No O(delta), universal editor ranking, bundle-size or release-ready claim. Structured Autoreview not run on next.
